questions.question: Faiyaz's birthday is on Wednesday 12th April. On what day of the week will be Shray's Birthday in the same year if Shray was born on 2ⁿd October?
questions.solution:
According to the question, 12th April is Wednesday.

Number of days left in April = 30 – 12 = 18.

Similarly, odd days from 12th April till 2ⁿd October = (18 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 31 + 30 + 2) / 7

= (4 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 2)/7 = 19/7 = 5

Thus, day on 2ⁿd October = Wednesday + 5 = Monday.

questions.question: The weights of 4 boxes are 20, 90, 40 and 60 kilograms. Which of the following cannot be the total weight, in kilograms, of any combination of these boxes and in a combination a box can be used only once?
If 45% 11 = 7, 59 % 34 = 7 then what is the value of 55 % 4 = ?
questions.solution:
The pattern followed is that the sum of digits of second number is subtracted from the sum of digits of first number.

45% 11 = (4 + 5) – (1 + 1) = 9 – 2 = 7 and

59% 34 = (5 + 9) – (3 + 4) = 14 – 7 = 7

Similarly, 55% 4 = (5 + 5) – (4) = 10 – 4 = 6

Hence, 6 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Two cars C and D start from the same point. C travels 9 km South, then turns to its left and travels another 11 km. D travels 3 km East, then turns South and travels 5 km, then turns to its left and travels another 8 km. Where is D with respect to C now?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5a0a03cc5b56963c945d8b60b4dd989817cab0da20de920f73b1bd8554d7165d.png] 

Let both C and D start from point R. C’s path is shown by black and D’s by blue.

C travels 9 km south and reaches S, then takes left turn and reaches point T by travelling 11 km.

Similarly, D travels east for 3 km and reaches Q, then turns south for 5 km and finally stops at point O.

Thus, OT = 9 – 5 = 4 km.

So, D is 4 km to the north of C.

questions.question:
**Directions:** In the question a statement is given, followed by two arguments, I and II. You have to consider the statement to be true even if it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given arguments, if any, is a strong argument.

**Statement:** Should street lights be switched off after midnight?

**Argument I:** No, statistics show that crime and accidents will increase if the street lights are switched off.

**Argument II: **Yes, since fewer vehicles ply after midnight, expensive electricity will be wasted.

options.text: Both I and II are strong.
Neither I nor II is strong.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1. Only argument I is strong. 

The first argument states that if lights are switched off after midnight, then it can result in increased crime and accidents, thus it is a strong argument as it has a direct impact on life of people.

Argument II, in comparison with argument I, is weaker as there are other ways to save electricity, such as switching to more efficient sources, managing the usage of electricity, etc. Switching off streetlights after midnight will increase the risk to human lives which cannot be allowed. Thus, argument II is not strong.

questions.question: The male sex accessory ducts include vasa efferentia, epididymis, vas deferens and______.
questions.solution:

questions.question: If at a price, market supply is greater than market demand, we say that there is ________ in the market at that price.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3, i.e., __Excess Supply__

 
• When there is a difference between the price that consumer pay in the market and the value that consumers place on the product, then the concept of consumer surplus becomes a useful one to look at. 
 
• Consumer surplus is a measure of the welfare that people gain from consuming goods and services
 
• Consumer surplus is defined as the difference between the total amount that consumers are willing and able to pay for a good or service (indicated by the demand curve) and the total amount that they actually do pay (i.e. the market price).

questions.question: D and E are points on side AB and AC of ΔABC. DE is parallel to BC. If AD : DB = 2 : 5 and area of ΔADE is 8 cm sq, what is the area (in sq cm) of quadrilateral BDEC?
questions.solution:
Here ΔADE and ΔABC are similar triangles

Given: AD/AB = 2/7

So, DE/BC = 2/7

Let DE be 2b. Then, BC will be 7b

Make an altitude from A on BC and mark the points P and R when it cuts DE and BC respectively.

So, ΔAPD and ΔARB are also similar triangles

⇒ AP/AR = 2/7

Let AP be 2b. Then, AR will be 7b

Since,

Area of ΔADE = 1/2 × 2a × 2b = 2ab

Area of ΔABC = 1/2 × 7a × 7b = 49ab/2

So, area of quadrilateral BDEC = 49ab/2 - 2ab = 45ab/2

∴ Required area = 45ab/2 × (8/2ab) = 90 cm²

questions.question: The distance between the points (2, 7) and (k, -5) is 13. What is the value of k?

**Given:**

Distance between the two points = 13

**Formulae used:**

Distance between 2 points = √{[(x₂ - x₁)²] + [(y₂ - y₁)²]}

**Calculations:**

According to question

(x₁,y₁) = (2, 7)

(x₂,y₂) = (k, -5) 

⇒ 13 = √{[(k - 2)²] + [(-5 - 7)²]}

⇒ 13 = √{[k² + 4 - 4k] + [144]}

⇒ 13 = √{k² - 4k + 148}

Squaring both sides

⇒ 169 = k² - 4k + 148

⇒ k² - 4k - 21 = 0

⇒ k² - 7k + 3k - 21 = 0

⇒ k(k - 7) + 3(k - 7) = 0

⇒ (k + 3)(k - 7) = 0

∴ k = -3,

questions.question: A Rs. 100 shirt is offered at 10% discount and a Rs. 300 pair of trousers at 20% discount. If Pritam bought 1 shirt and 3 pairs of trousers, what is the effective discount (in %) he got?
questions.solution:
**Formula used:**

Discount = Marked Price - Selling price

Discount% = [(Marked Price - Selling price)/Marked price]× 100

**Calculation:**

Discount for one shirt = 100(10/100) = Rs 10

Discount for 3 pairs of trousers = 3 × 300(20/100) = Rs 180

Total discount = 10 + 180 = Rs 190

Total cost = 100 + 3 × 300 = 1000

For Rs 1000 he gets a discount of Rs 190

Effective discount % = 100 x (190 / 1000) = 19

∴ ∴ Total discount percentage = 19%

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

Total cost price of shirts and trousers = 100 × 1 + 300 × 3 = ₹1000

Discunted price for shirt = 100 × 90/100 = ₹90

Discounted price of trousers = 300 × 80/100 = ₹240

Total discounted price of trousers = 3 × 240 = ₹720

Total price paid = 90 + 720 = ₹810

Total discount = 1000 - 810 = 190

∴ Total discount percentage = 190/1000 × 100 = 19

questions.question: The 7th and 12th term of an arithmetic progression are -15 and 5 respectively. What is the 16th term?

Let the first term of A.P. be a and let the difference be d

⇒ a + 11d = 5 ----(ii)

Subtracting (i) from (ii)

⇒ 5d = 20

⇒ d = 4

Putting the value of d in (i)

⇒ a + 6 × 4 = -15

⇒ a = -15 - 24 = -39

So, 16th term = a + 15d = -39 + 15 × 4 = -39 + 60 = 21

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Active/Passive Voice.**

Who taught you to ride?

options.text: By whom is you taught to ride?
By whom were you taught to ride?
Riding by you was taught by who?
Riding by you was taught by whom?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2.

The given sentence is in the Active Voice as the form of the verb (‘taught’) shows that its subject (‘you’) did something and was ‘active’.

Therefore, it has to be changed to the Passive voice, where something was done by the subject, and it was ‘passive’.

In order to do that,

a. The object of the transitive verb (the verb which uses more than one objects) in the Active voice should become the subject of the verb in the Passive voice.

b. The verb should be changed from the Active voice to the Passive voice without changing its tense.

Thus, the same sentence in the Passive voice is **‘By whom were you taught to ride?'**

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

Sheetal said to me, "How have you solved this problem?"

options.text: Sheetal asked me how I had solved that problem.
Sheetal asked me how I have solved that problem.
Sheetal asked me how I had solved this problem.
Sheetal asked me how I have solved this problem.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sheetal asked me how I had solved that problem. **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let us begin by identifying the kind of sentence. It is an interrogative sentence. (Wh-Question)
 
• The reporting verb ‘said to’ should be changed as ‘asked’ in indirect speech.
 
• Following that, we need to remove the commas and inverted commas as we change it into an indirect speech.
 
• The Question is changed into assertive form and is simply placed after the reporting verb.
 
• The question mark is also removed.

Correct answer: *Sheetal asked me how I had solved that problem. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

When changing a direct speech to indirect speech:

 
• The words of the speaker are not enclosed in inverted commas.
 
• The conjunction ‘that’ will not be used. (In case of interrogative sentence)
 
• To make an indirect speech of Wh -Questions, The Question is changed into assertive form and is simply placed after the reporting verb.
 
• To make an indirect speech of YES/NO-Questions, if or whether will be used.
 
• The question mark is also removed.
 
• e.g., DIRECT: He said to me, “Will you help me?”

 INDIRECT: He asked me if I would help him.

 
• DIRECT: He said to me, “Why are you late?”

 INDIRECT: He asked me why I am late.

**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

Those films (being) made now.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3.

Since 'films' are plural, we know that the plural form of the verb 'be' will be used.

Hence, the sentence would be:

Those films **are being** made now.
